trajectory_summary: The customer arrives already knowledgeable, impatient, and unwilling to sit through a discovery call — he wants a price and panel count via email and says so almost immediately. The rep never secures the bill, never books an appointment, and spends the whole call trying to preserve the standard funnel format instead of adapting to what the customer actually asked for, ending in a polite but final decline.

observed_outcome.quote: No worries, brother. I appreciate your time. You have a good rest of your day.
observed_outcome.reasoning: The call ends with the customer declining to continue under the rep's terms and no appointment, callback time, or confirmed email exchange locked in.

bill_anchor_audit.reasoning: The customer references his 'PNM bill' repeatedly as something he's willing to send, but no dollar amount or usage figure is ever stated on the call, so there is nothing numeric to flip.

bill_document_audit.ask_quote: so you could determine how many panels I need based upon the, energy that I, need to be producing
bill_document_audit.result_quote: I'll give you my email, and, you can email me, and I'll send you all the info that you need.
bill_document_audit.reasoning: The customer himself raises sending the PNM bill via email multiple times; the rep never accepts this offer or sets up the email exchange, so the bill is promised by the customer but the exchange is never actually completed or confirmed by the rep before the call ends.

interest_reason_audit.reason_quote: I know plenty about solar, so I'm not worried about any of that. I just wanna know what price you guys can get me at
interest_reason_audit.reasoning: The rep never explicitly asks 'what interested you in solar,' but the customer volunteers his motivation (wants price/panel-count numbers, already knowledgeable) unprompted; the rep never reflects this back or uses it to frame the call ('since you already know the numbers matter most, let's get you that fast') — he instead keeps re-arguing the format.

primary_coaching_focus.topic: repeating the same channel argument instead of using the customer's own words
primary_coaching_focus.quote: To be real, brother, I don't wanna waste anybody's time. That's why I said via email.
primary_coaching_focus.why: The rep hears the customer state his reason for wanting email twice (impatience, already solar-literate, wants numbers) and responds both times with variations of 'we're the best' or policy citations rather than mirroring the customer's stated motivation back into a reason to stay on the phone. This is the single biggest lever this call needed and never got pulled.

key_moments.quote: I can tell people. You gotta be stupid to take from me.
key_moments.stewart_read: This pre-intro fragment (likely mid-conversation with someone else before the call connects, or a defensive aside) suggests the customer has a guarded, transaction-skeptical posture before the rep even speaks. It sets up his fast pivot to 'can this be done via email' as consistent with someone who doesn't want to be worked.

key_moments.quote: I don't need all the other stuff. I'll look at it. If it looks good and everything is good to go, then, obviously, I'll choose you guys to get services with.
key_moments.stewart_read: The customer is essentially pre-committing to buy if the numbers work — this is close to a self-generated 'what's expensive is not switching' opening, and the rep never uses the customer's own conditional commitment as leverage to get him on a call instead of email.

key_moments.quote: Yeah. No. I mean and that's what everybody says. You know what I mean? Like, I I I've been in sales, and I and I used to sell for solar too.
key_moments.stewart_read: The customer discloses direct competitive/industry background (worked in solar sales himself) and that he's already talked to multiple solar companies — this is exactly the kind of prior-contact disclosure the verify section's prior_designs item is built to capture, and the rep does not probe which companies or what he was shown.

key_moments.quote: So that's why I said I I just if I can just email you the p and m Mhmm. So you can go ahead and review it.
key_moments.stewart_read: The customer hands the rep his own PNM bill and satellite-imagery point as an anchor — a direct hook the rep could reflect back ('once we pull that, our specialist can show you the actual number live') to make phone conversation more attractive than email. Instead the rep files it and continues repeating the appointment-format ask.
